details: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has begun phasing out withdrawals on November 1, 2026, after experiencing a record-breaking $6.3 billion hack. The FBI has officially attributed the attack to "TraderTraitor," a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group. Binance stated it has replenished 90-95% of the stolen assets and affirmed its commitment to fully cover all user losses through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). The incident initially triggered a significant market sell-off, causing Bitcoin to drop below $77,000 and Ethereum to fall to around $2,200.
title: Binance Resumes Withdrawals After $6.3B Hack; FBI Blames North Korea

details: The overall cryptocurrency market saw a substantial $360 billion reduction in value during October 2026, bringing its total market capitalization to approximately $2.63 trillion. Bitcoin, the leading cryptocurrency, fell 7.3% to close the month at around $77,424, marking its weakest October performance since 2016. Dogecoin was among the hardest-hit top-ten cryptocurrencies. This market downturn was primarily attributed to lingering concerns over Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, significant outflows of $2.1 billion from Bitcoin and Ethereum Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), and the recent Binance security breach. Despite the challenging October, Bitcoin has shown signs of recovery towards $78,000 and Ethereum above $2,250 on November 1.
title: Crypto Market Sheds $360B in October Amid Fed & Binance Hack

details: On October 31, 2026, a "Halloween attack" targeted at least 12 Decentralized Finance (DeFi) websites, utilizing a malicious toolkit identified as "Step Drainer." Blockchain security firm Blockaid detected the exploit and issued warnings for users to avoid connecting their wallets or signing suspicious transactions on affected platforms, which included Flap and Kintsu. Preliminary on-chain analysis indicates that approximately $138,000 in assets were suspected to be stolen, with investigations revealing that all compromised domains were registered through Name.com.
title: DeFi DNS Attack Hits 12 Sites, 'Step Drainer' Toolkit Identified

details: From October 26 to November 1, 2026, Ethereum's DeFi contracts experienced a significant outflow of 1.39 million ETH, valued at approximately $3.16 billion. This 6.7% drop represents the first genuine outflow from DeFi since late September. Conversely, Ethereum's staking activity continues its robust growth, with nearly 43.8 million ETH, or 35.9% of the total circulating supply, now locked in the consensus layer, supported by an impressive 814,000 active validators.
title: Ethereum DeFi Contracts See $3.16B Outflow, Staking Hits Record Highs

details: The total supply of stablecoins in the market has decreased by $3.1 billion since October 28, reaching $29.85 billion on November 1, 2026. This marks the lowest stablecoin supply level recorded since August 2026 and represents a $5.2 billion reduction from January 1, 2026, effectively reversing earlier market gains. The yearly peak for stablecoin supply was noted on May 17 at $31.55 billion.
title: Stablecoin Supply Falls to $29.85 Billion, Lowest Since August

details: The volume of tokenized stocks on the Ethereum network experienced a remarkable surge of 170% over the past year, reaching $827 million by the close of October 2026. This substantial growth underscores the increasing maturity of the real-world assets (RWA) sector, which is progressively moving beyond its experimental phase. Ethereum's well-established and liquid infrastructure, currently dominating over 53% of the global stablecoin market, is proving to be a pivotal channel for the digitization of traditional equities.
title: Ethereum Tokenized Equities Surge 170% to $827M by October End
